brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Hex base cells at level 0 (0,0 full; 1,0 half-e; 0,1 full) and level 1 (0,0 full; 1,0 half-e; 0,1 full), stacked and joined, with open faces capped and joints locked. check_build is ok with meshClash clear.
Built as a compact hex tower of 49 parts (about 2.9 kg of filament estimated). Its footprint is small; I did not check it against a particular bench size, and it has no mounting to the bench.

Two notch drawer frames (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf): one at level 0 cell (-1,1,0) between bases (0,0) and (0,1), one at level 1 cell (-1,1,1) between bases (0,0,1) and (0,1,1). Drawer frames are placed; no drawer contents were added.

finish.summary: Built a two-storey hex tower: two stacked storeys of bases with two notch drawer frames, one per storey. Open faces are capped and joints locked; the configurator reports no issues and a clear mesh check. Drawers are the frame type and I did not add bin contents. The tower is 49 parts, above the usual 40-part guideline, because two drawers per storey needed the extra bases.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
